title: Tools and protocol for quantification of myosin phosphorylation with MRM-MS
author: MacDonald, Ulke-Lemée, et al.
materials: •TCA/DTT/acetone: 10% (w/v) trichloroacetic acid, 10 mM dithiothreitol in ice cold acetone.•DTT/acetone: 10 mM dithiothreitol in ice cold acetone•Lyophiliser- Freeze Dry System (Labconco, Freezone 6)•Tissue extraction buffer: 50 mM ABC, pH 8.2, 50 mM NaCl, 1 M urea, 2% (w/v) sodium deoxycholate, 1 mM DTT and cOmplete protease inhibitor cocktail (Millipore-Sigma). LC20 is primarily associated with the insoluble fraction during isolation of muscle proteins with centrifugation, so we include of 2% (w/v) sodium deoxycholate and 1 M urea to enhance the solubilization efficiency.•Micro ground-glass, Potter-Elvehjem tissue homogenizer•Vortex shaker•Refrigerated micro-centrifuge

steps.title: Gather reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all chemicals, solutions and hardware listed for the assay: 10 % (w/v) trichloroacetic acid (TCA), 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), ice‑cold acetone, lyophiliser (Labconco Freezone 6), tissue extraction buffer (50 mM ABC, pH 8.2, 50 mM NaCl, 1 M urea, 2 % w/v sodium deoxycholate, 1 mM DTT, cOmplete protease inhibitor cocktail), micro ground‑glass Potter‑Elvehjem homogenizer, vortex shaker, refrigerated micro‑centrifuge, BCA protein assay kit, HEPES pH 7.4 (200 mM), CaCl₂ (100 mM), LC20 stock (4 mg ml⁻¹), calmodulin (5 mg ml⁻¹), ATP (100 mM), MgCl₂ (100 mM), MLCK (1 mg ml⁻¹), EDTA/EGTA quench solution (126 mM EDTA, 73 mM EGTA), Analyst software, Skyline software, Dionex HPLC system, trap and analytical columns, 5 % ACN/0.5 % TFA solution, 15 µl injection vials, and appropriate pipettes.

steps.title: Generate phosphorylated LC20 standards
steps.instruction: Prepare two in‑vitro kinase reactions to obtain mono‑ and diphosphorylated LC20 as follows:

substeps.instruction: For each 300 µl reaction, add 25 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 0.1 mM CaCl₂, and 20 µg LC20 (from 4 mg ml⁻¹ stock).
Add calmodulin: 10 µg ml⁻¹ for the mono‑phosphorylation (LC20‑1P) reaction, 20 µg ml⁻¹ for the diphosphorylation (LC20‑2P) reaction.
Add ATP to a final concentration of 0.2 mM (from 100 mM stock).
Add MgCl₂ to a final concentration of 2 mM (from 100 mM stock).
Vortex gently to mix.

Initiate the reaction by adding MgCl₂‑ATP solution (as above) followed immediately by MLCK: add 1 µg ml⁻¹ MLCK for the mono‑phosphorylation reaction and 60 µg ml⁻¹ MLCK for the diphosphorylation reaction.
Incubate at 30 °C: 1–5 min for mono‑phosphorylation (promotes pS19 only) and 45–60 min for diphosphorylation (pT18 + pS19).
Terminate the reaction by adding 21.6 µl of the quench buffer (126 mM EDTA, 73 mM EGTA).

steps.title: Lyophilise and store smooth muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry smooth muscle strips for at least 16 h, then store at –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Extract proteins from tissue
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen tissue on ice and extract proteins with ice‑cold buffer as described:

substeps.instruction: Remove lyophilised strips from –80 °C and keep on ice.

Immediately add ice‑cold extraction buffer (50 mM ABC pH 8.2, 50 mM NaCl, 1 M urea, 2 % w/v sodium deoxycholate, 1 mM DTT, protease inhibitor cocktail). Use 0.25 ml per rat caudal artery strip (~6 mg tissue) or 0.1 ml per rat ileal strip (~2.5 mg tissue).
Homogenise each strip with a micro Potter‑Elvehjem homogeniser, ensuring the tissue remains fully immersed in buffer.
Transfer the homogenate to a 0.5 ml micro‑centrifuge tube.
Vortex the tube for 2 h at 5 °C.
Centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 10 min at 5 °C to clarify the extract.
Determine protein concentration of the supernatant using a BCA assay.

steps.title: Create Analyst MRM method
steps.instruction: In Analyst, build a new MRM method using the transition list from Table 2, selecting “MRM Method” and enabling “Scheduling”. Ensure the table format matches the provided precursor (Q1) and fragment (Q3) masses, charge states and other parameters.

steps.title: Configure Skyline and HPLC for MRM‑MS
steps.instruction: Set up the LC‑MS acquisition as follows:

substeps.instruction: Create a “Dionex Chromatography MS Link” HPLC program with a trap column operated in reverse‑elution mode.
Set flow rate to 50 µl min⁻¹ and a linear gradient from 2 % to 50 % (v/v) acetonitrile containing 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid.
Select a 10 min MRM detection window for each peptide (initially wide to accommodate retention‑time drift).
Use partial‑inject mode with a 15 µl injection volume.
Load samples into the autosampler, checking for air bubbles.
Inject 5 % ACN / 0.5 % TFA as the first run to equilibrate the system.
Load any phosphorylated LC20 protein standard last to avoid bleed‑through.

steps.title: Run MRM‑MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Execute the batch run on the mass spectrometer using the Analyst method and HPLC program prepared above, collecting *.wiff files for each sample.

steps.title: Import data into Skyline
steps.instruction: Open Skyline, import each *.wiff file, and verify that the LC20‑0P, LC20‑1P, LC20‑2P and pan‑LC20 (GNFNYVEFTR) precursor ions and their transitions are displayed.

steps.title: Quantify peak areas
steps.instruction: For each sample, use Skyline’s automatic background subtraction to obtain peak areas for the three diagnostic transitions of LC20‑0P, LC20‑1P and LC20‑2P.

substeps.instruction: Export the peak‑area table to Microsoft Excel.
Sum the three transition areas for each precursor peptide.
Calculate LC20 phosphorylation stoichiometry in Excel using the equation supplied in the original manuscript (stoichiometry = [sum of p‑peptide areas] / [sum of all peptide areas]).
